title: MARITRAUMA - Injury patterns, outcomes, and microbiological pathogens in ship, boat, and propeller injuries
summary: Injuries caused by ship propellers are among the most serious accidents around bodies of water and are associated with high rates of severe complications and mortality. These injuries frequently lead to wound infections, which can involve both common and unusual bacteria from freshwater, seawater, and soil. A 10-year retrospective evaluation can provide important insights into typical injury patterns, infection risks, healing processes, and preventive measures. The aim of the present study is therefore to establish a systematic recording and evaluation of injuries caused by ships, boats, and propellers in order to accurately describe their frequency, severity, injury patterns, risk factors, as well as the procedures in initial emergency care and in the hospital.
conditions: Patients with injuries caused by ships, boats, or propellers

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients with documented injuries caused by ships, boats, or propellers who were treated at the BG Klinikum Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin between 01/2016 and 08/2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- All patients with documented injuries caused by ships, boats, or propellers in the emergency department report or in the EPIAS documentation from 01/2016 to 08/2026
- Presentation to the emergency department of the BG Klinikum Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin during the study period
- Availability of the emergency department report and at least one additional document, such as an operative report, microbiological finding, or radiological finding
Exclusion criteria:
- Incomplete documentation without usable data
- Everyday injuries/minor injuries without a direct connection to a boat, ship, or propeller (e.g., misstep during shore leave on a cruise, fall down the stairs on a cruise ship, etc.)
